title: Expand static_sanity.py audit to continuous monitoring daemon
why: The static_sanity module currently checks only 14 critical modules at startup; a complete audit of all 1807 files found 42+ undefined-name bugs (including blocker_quarantine:max_depth crash-loop, missing functions in config_sync/ci_dispatch). Silent NameErrors hide for days (3-day 'zero merged' incident), costing observability and incident time.
value: Prevent cascading silent crashes by catching undefined-name bugs before runtime; estimated 5-10 preventable incidents per quarter (NameError, AttributeError from dropped definitions).
risk: Fail-soft if pyflakes unavailable (already implemented); monitor adds ~2% CPU to periodic heartbeat. Test plan: (1) run audit() on full tree and verify 42+ findings surface, (2) integrate into intake_watcher loop with sub-second overhead, (3) assert critical modules clean at startup as today, (4) add 20+ unit tests for edge cases (directories, permissions, missing tool).

title: Consolidate nested import patterns into safe_import() utility
why: merge_train.py, release_train.py, and ~50 other import sites use nested try/except blocks (lines 42-52 of merge_train.py: 3 levels deep, 4 fallback strategies) to handle optional modules. This pattern is repeated identically across multiple files, creates code smell, and obscures the intended fallback chain. Two recent NameErrors (repo_lock, concurrent.futures never imported) suggest the pattern is error-prone.
value: Reduce import boilerplate by ~30 lines per module; improve clarity of import fallbacks; reduce likelihood of missing-import NameErrors by consolidating logic into one tested place.
risk: Refactor risk: must verify all 50+ call sites handle ImportError identically before/after. Test plan: (1) create safe_import(name, optional=False) utility, (2) refactor merge_train.py:_load_guard() and 10 other critical sites, (3) run full test suite to verify no regressions, (4) add 15 unit tests covering ImportError, ModuleNotFoundError, missing packages.

title: Add structured logging to 4297 silent exception handlers
why: 4297 exception handlers across the codebase contain bare `except Exception: pass` or silent catch-and-continue patterns. Examples: account_pool.py (lines 107-116), adaptive_pipeline.py (lines 85-88). This masks real failures and makes post-incident debugging impossible. Recent incidents (NameError crash-loops) went undiagnosed for days because exceptions were silently swallowed.
value: Transform silent crashes into observable events; enable rapid root-cause diagnosis. Estimated 30-50% faster MTTR on production incidents by capturing exception context (type, message, traceback location).
risk: Log spam if handlers catch too broad; solution: use module-level debug logger with context-aware severity (ERROR for unexpected, DEBUG for expected transient failures). Test plan: (1) identify 50 high-value sites (db operations, subprocess calls, file I/O), (2) add structured logging with exception type and call context, (3) run 1-week production shadow mode, verify log volume acceptable (<5% increase), (4) add 25+ unit tests asserting logs captured on each handler type.
